parts.gloss: without leaving (constantly remaining in the mind)
do not set / do not disappear

literal: Without leaving him who departed, with my eyes to see, do not set, live long, O Moon!
translation: May you live long, O Moon! Do not set yet, so that I may behold with my own eyes him who departed from me but has never left my heart.
modern: என் நெஞ்சை விட்டு நீங்காமல் பிரிந்து சென்றவரை என் கண்களால் காணும் வரை, நிலவே! நீ மறையாமல் இருப்பாயாக; நீ வாழ்க!
explanation: In this verse, the pining heroine addresses the moon. She speaks of her lover as one who has departed physically but has never left her thoughts. She pleads with the moon not to set just yet, wishing it a long life, so that she may have enough light to see him with her own eyes. The use of the lengthened phonetic forms 'விடாஅது' and 'படாஅதி' emphasizes her deep, lingering distress and her urgent plea to the moon.
